title: Understanding OLS
text: In an Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) model, the goal is to minimize the sum of the squared differences between the observed values and the values predicted by the model. This is achieved by finding the optimal weight vector, often denoted as theta.

title: Residuals and Orthogonality
text: The residual vector, often denoted as e, represents the difference between the observed values and the predicted values. In OLS, this residual vector is orthogonal to the span of the design matrix X. This means that the dot product of e with any vector in the span of X is zero.

hintAnswer: The residual vector e is orthogonal to the span of X.
title: Dimensionality Check
text: Consider the dimensions of Y and the weight vector theta. Which of the following statements is true?
choices: Y and theta have the same dimensionality.
The residual vector e is orthogonal to the span of X.
The prediction vector $$Y_{hat}$$ is orthogonal to the span of X.
